intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

selected_hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Guided game drives allow you to observe elephants, giraffes, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species in open savannah landscapes with iconic snow-capped mountain views.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided walking safaris and jeep tours let you track rhinos on foot with expert rangers, offering an intimate and educational wildlife conservation experience unlike any traditional game drive.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Discover the breathtaking pink shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting millions of flamingos along with pelicans, African fish eagles, and over 450 bird species. The park also shelters white and black rhinos, lions, leopards, and Rothschild giraffes in a compact and highly rewarding ecosystem.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk
experiences.description: Spend a half-day with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Maasai Mara to learn about their ancient wildlife coexistence practices, traditional medicine from native plants, and warrior customs. A guided bush walk with a Maasai elder reveals how to track animals, identify edible plants, and understand the deep cultural connection between the Maasai people and Kenya's wildlife.
experiences.location: Maasai Villages, Narok County border of Maasai Mara

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange shared shuttle or budget matatu transfer toward Narok County (approximately 5–6 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your Boutique Stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve area. Check in, freshen up, and take a short walk around the lodge grounds at dusk to spot nocturnal wildlife beginning to stir. Attend a brief orientation session hosted by lodge staff about the reserve rules and upcoming activities.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport — budget KES 300–500 at airport kiosks.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple road snack or stop at a local roadside 'mama mboga' food stall along the Narok highway — ugali, sukuma wiki, and chicken for around KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the lodge's communal dining area — many budget boutique stays include a simple set dinner. Expect nyama choma (roasted meat), rice, and vegetables for KES 800–1,200 if not included.

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle in advance to save costs — shared transfers from Nairobi to Maasai Mara run KES 1,500–2,500 per person versus KES 15,000+ for a private vehicle. Carry KES cash as ATMs are scarce near the reserve.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for an early morning game drive departing at 06:00. July is peak season for the Great Migration — witness massive wildebeest and zebra herds moving across the savannah. Look for the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. Shared game drive vehicles from budget camps cost KES 3,000–4,500 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp by 11:00 for brunch. Rest during the hottest part of the day (12:00–15:00). At 15:30 head out for an afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — lions are most active hunting in late afternoon. Spot cheetahs on open plains and hippos at the Mara River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp at sunset (around 18:30). Gather around the campfire for a traditional Maasai storytelling session arranged by the lodge. Learn about Maasai culture, wildlife tracking, and conservation efforts. Star-gazing in the clear July sky afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-drive tea and biscuits at the lodge, then a full bush breakfast of eggs, toast, fruit, and chai on return — typically included in lodge packages or KES 400–600.
meals.lunch: Simple packed lunch or lodge buffet — ugali, lentil stew, chapati, and fresh fruit for KES 500–700.
meals.dinner: Communal campfire dinner at the lodge — grilled chicken, roasted vegetables, and ugali. Budget KES 800–1,000 if not included in your stay.

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) on game drives. Avoid bright colors and strong perfumes. Bring a light fleece jacket — early mornings in July can drop to 12–15°C despite warm daytime temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive at 06:00 with a focus on the Mara River crossing points. July is prime wildebeest river crossing season — one of nature's greatest spectacles. Position near Crossing Points 1 or 4 with your guide for the best vantage. Crossings are unpredictable so patience is key.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning to camp, enjoy a guided nature walk around the lodge perimeter (KES 500–800 per person with a Maasai guide). Learn to identify animal tracks, medicinal plants, and bird species. The Mara hosts over 450 bird species — look for lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and African fish eagles.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby authentic Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural experience. Watch traditional jumping dances, tour a traditional homestead, and purchase handcrafted beaded jewelry directly from artisans. Costs around KES 1,000–1,500 per person — negotiate respectfully and buy crafts to support the community.

meals.breakfast: Pre-drive tea and a hearty lodge breakfast on return — eggs, porridge, fruit, and mandazi (Kenyan doughnuts). Budget KES 400–500.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp — bean soup, chapati, and salad. KES 400–600.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Maasai village or back at camp. Try nyama choma with kachumbari (tomato-onion salsa) and ugali — a quintessential Kenyan meal. KES 700–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Tip your game drive driver-guide KES 500–1,000 per day — they are knowledgeable professionals and tips form a significant part of their income. Always ask permission before photographing Maasai community members.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive starting at 06:00 exploring the Mara Triangle — the western section of the reserve managed by the Mara Conservancy, known for fewer crowds and excellent wildlife density. Look for large elephant herds, lion prides, and the elusive leopard resting in acacia trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the full-day drive with a packed bush picnic lunch eaten in the vehicle or at a designated picnic site. Explore the Oloololo Escarpment area for panoramic views of the Mara ecosystem and spot hyena dens and wild dog activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 18:30. Attend a free sunset photography session — the golden hour light over the Mara plains is spectacular. Share photos and stories with fellow travelers at the communal lounge. Early night to rest for upcoming activities.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-drive snack — tea, fruit, and a boiled egg. KES 200–300.
meals.lunch: Packed bush picnic prepared by the lodge — sandwiches, fruit, juice, and a snack bar. Typically included in full-day drive packages or KES 500 extra.
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner — slow-cooked beef stew, rice, steamed greens, and fresh mango. KES 800–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: A full-day shared game drive in the Mara Triangle costs approximately KES 4,000–6,000 per person including park fees. Book through your lodge to get the best group rate. Carry at least 2 liters of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in until 07:30 and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning at the lodge doing wildlife journaling, sketching, or reviewing your photographs. Attend a free bird-watching session led by a lodge guide around the camp's water source and acacia woodland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive from 15:30 focusing on the Talek River area — excellent for hippo pods, crocodiles, and waterbirds. Watch elephants bathing and drinking at sunset. Spot the iconic silhouette of a giraffe against the orange sky.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner experience — bring a drink to a scenic hilltop viewpoint and watch the sun set over the Mara. Many budget lodges offer this as a complimentary activity. Return for dinner and a relaxed evening under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — fresh fruit, porridge, eggs to order, toast, and Kenyan chai. KES 400–600.
meals.lunch: Self-catered light lunch at the lodge — buy fresh fruit, bread, and peanut butter from the lodge kitchen or nearby Talek village market for KES 300–400.
meals.dinner: Lodge communal dinner — fish curry (tilapia), coconut rice, and sukuma wiki. Fresh passion fruit juice. KES 700–900.

day_by_day.notes: Talek village, just outside the reserve gate, has small dukas (shops) where you can buy snacks, water, and basic supplies at much lower prices than inside the reserve. Stock up here to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning balloon safari alternative — if budget allows, a hot air balloon over the Mara costs USD 450–500 per person, which may be outside strict budget. Instead, opt for a guided walking safari at dawn (KES 1,500–2,000 per person) — walk through the savannah with an armed Maasai ranger and experience the bush at ground level.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Olare Motorogi Conservancy buffer zone adjacent to the reserve for a quieter game drive experience. Conservancy fees are often lower and wildlife is equally impressive with fewer vehicles. Look for wild dogs, servals, and rare antelope species like roan and eland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a community conservation talk hosted by a local ranger or conservancy officer — learn about anti-poaching efforts, human-wildlife conflict mitigation, and how tourism revenue protects the ecosystem. Free activity arranged through the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Pre-walk tea and light snack. Full breakfast on return — KES 400–500.
meals.lunch: Lodge buffet lunch — mixed bean salad, chapati, grilled chicken, and fruit. KES 500–700.
meals.dinner: Special budget 'braai night' at the lodge — communal outdoor barbecue with nyama choma, roasted maize, and kachumbari. KES 800–1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris must be done with a licensed armed ranger — never walk alone in the reserve. This is one of the most intimate wildlife experiences available and highly recommended for nature enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Early game drive at 06:00 with a specific focus on big cat tracking. July is excellent for cheetah sightings on the open Mara plains. Your guide will radio-network with other drivers to locate active sightings. Spend time observing lion pride dynamics and cub behavior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara Elephant Project information center (if accessible from your lodge) to learn about elephant tracking and conservation. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the lodge's pool or rest area before a late afternoon bird walk along the river with your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cultural dinner — arrange with the lodge for a traditional Kenyan feast featuring irio (mashed peas, potato, and corn), pilau rice, grilled tilapia, and chapati. Celebrate the week's wildlife sightings with fellow travelers. Share a communal pot of Kenyan chai.

meals.breakfast: Pre-drive tea and biscuits, full breakfast on return. KES 400–500.
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch — vegetable soup, bread, and fresh juice. KES 400–500.
meals.dinner: Traditional Kenyan cultural dinner at the lodge — KES 1,000–1,500 for a special spread. Worth the splurge on the final Mara evening.

day_by_day.notes: Start organizing your departure logistics — confirm your shared transfer booking back to Nairobi for Day 8 or 9. Settle any outstanding lodge bills and exchange any remaining lodge credits.

day_by_day.morning: Final early morning game drive at 06:00 — a last chance to witness the Great Migration and say goodbye to the Mara. Capture final photographs and take in the landscape. Return to camp by 09:30 for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Boutique Stay and board your shared transfer back toward Nairobi (departing around 10:00–11:00, arriving Nairobi 16:00–17:00). Stop at the Rift Valley viewpoint for panoramic photos — a stunning natural landmark on the Nairobi-Narok highway. Explore Nairobi's budget-friendly Westlands or Ngara area upon arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Nairobi (KES 1,500–2,500 per night — options include Upper Hill Campsite, Kenya Comfort Hotel, or Milimani Backpackers). Explore the lively Nairobi streets, visit a local market, and enjoy the city's energy after days in the bush.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — make it count! KES 400–600.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop lunch on the Narok highway — local restaurant serving pilau, nyama choma, and chapati for KES 300–500.
meals.dinner: Nairobi budget dinner at a local nyama choma joint or Indian restaurant in Westlands — KES 600–900. Try Carnivore restaurant's budget lunch menu or a local kibanda (street food stall).

day_by_day.notes: Nairobi traffic can be severe in the late afternoon — plan your arrival time accordingly. Keep your valuables secure in Nairobi and use reputable taxis or Bolt/Uber app rather than unmarked cabs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nairobi National Park — the world's only national park within a capital city. Entry costs KES 4,306 for non-residents or significantly less for residents. Take a shared matatu to the park gate and join a shared game drive. Spot lions, giraffes, rhinos, and over 400 bird species against the Nairobi skyline backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (open to visitors 11:00–12:00 daily, USD 7 entry — approximately KES 900). Watch baby elephants being fed and learn about their rescue and rehabilitation. Walk to the nearby Giraffe Centre (KES 1,500 entry) to hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Maasai Market at Village Market or Yaya Centre (held on Fridays) for authentic Kenyan crafts, beaded jewelry, carvings, and textiles at negotiable prices. Great for budget souvenirs. Return to your guesthouse for a relaxed final evening.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — mandazi, chai, and eggs for KES 200–350.
meals.lunch: Java House or Artcaffe for a mid-range budget meal — sandwiches and fresh juice for KES 700–1,000, or a local kibanda for KES 300–400.
meals.dinner: Nairobi local restaurant dinner — try Ethiopian cuisine at a Westlands restaurant (injera with various stews) for KES 700–1,000, or a Kenyan buffet at a local hotel for KES 500–800.

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Market prices are always negotiable — start at 40–50% of the asking price and work up. Buying multiple items from one vendor often yields better discounts. Keep receipts for any wildlife products to avoid customs issues.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya — visit the Karen Blixen Museum (KES 1,200 entry) in the leafy Karen suburb, the former home of the 'Out of Africa' author, surrounded by beautiful colonial gardens. Alternatively, explore the Nairobi Arboretum (KES 200 entry) for a peaceful nature walk among indigenous trees and birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Utamaduni Craft Centre in Karen or the City Market in central Nairobi. Pack your bags and arrange an airport transfer — use Uber/Bolt (KES 800–1,200) or a pre-booked shuttle (KES 500–700 shared) to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Arrive at least 3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Kenya budget safari — the Great Migration, Big Five sightings, Maasai culture, and the raw beauty of the Mara. Check in for your flight and enjoy duty-free browsing at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse final breakfast or Java House — chai, eggs, and toast for KES 300–500.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Karen or City Market — quick chapati and beans or a sandwich for KES 300–500.
meals.dinner: Airport dining — budget for KES 1,000–1,500 at JKIA restaurants, or eat before heading to the airport to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 10 days excluding flights: KES 45,000–70,000 (approximately USD 350–550) covering accommodation, shared game drives, park fees, meals, and transfers. The Maasai Mara experience alone is worth every shilling — Kenya's wildlife is unmatched in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer driver in the arrivals hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Nairobi for Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours by road via the scenic Rift Valley escarpment). Stop at a viewpoint along the Rift Valley for photos and a short stretch break. Arrive at your boutique stay in the Mara by early evening and complete check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your boutique lodge, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome briefing from your camp manager about the days ahead. Take a relaxed sundowner drink on the lodge terrace overlooking the savannah as the golden hour sets in.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport before landing
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a roadside café or packed snack box arranged by your transfer driver along the Nairobi–Mara highway
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique lodge restaurant — enjoy a set Kenyan menu featuring nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, and seasonal vegetables; mid-range lodge dining included or budgeted at KES 2,000–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your road transfer from Nairobi in advance. Alternatively, a 45-minute charter flight from Wilson Airport to Mara airstrips (Keekorok or Ol Kiombo) is available for a faster arrival and fits a mid-range budget upgrade. Carry light layers for the evening — temperatures can drop to 15°C after sunset in July.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise at 06:00 for your first full-day game drive in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Head out with your guide at dawn to catch predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are most active at first light. Explore the Mara Triangle and Musiara Marsh areas, prime zones for big cat sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your game drive through the open savannah, scanning for elephant herds, buffalo, giraffes, and hippos along the Mara River. Break for a bush picnic lunch prepared by your lodge in a scenic spot inside the reserve. Return to camp by 16:00 for rest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a guided nature walk around the lodge perimeter with a Maasai guide to learn about local flora, tracks, and bush survival skills. Return for dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at the lodge before departure — eggs, fresh fruit, toast, and Kenyan chai tea
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch box provided by the lodge inside the reserve — sandwiches, fruit, juice, and snacks
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the lodge — try the slow-cooked lamb stew or grilled tilapia with kachumbari salad; budget KES 2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — wildebeest river crossings at the Mara River are highly likely this month. Ask your guide to position you at a crossing point early. Bring binoculars, sunscreen, and a wide-brimmed hat. Park entry fees (approximately USD 80 per person per day) should be pre-paid or budgeted.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — dedicated full morning game drive focused on the Great Migration spectacle. Join millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles as they move across the Mara ecosystem. Position with your guide near the Mara River for a chance to witness a dramatic river crossing with crocodiles in pursuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning crossing experience, drive through the Serena and Governors' Camp areas of the Mara for more wildlife encounters. Spot hyenas, jackals, and vultures feeding near recent kills — a raw and authentic wildlife experience. Return to lodge for a late lunch and afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Optional sundowner game drive at 17:00 — watch the savannah transform in golden light and spot nocturnal animals beginning to stir, including aardvarks and genets. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the lodge — eggs your way, sausages, fresh tropical fruit platter, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge after return — buffet-style with salads, grilled meats, and local stews; included in most lodge packages
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — enjoy a three-course meal with soup, main (beef tenderloin or vegetarian option), and dessert; budget KES 3,000–4,500

day_by_day.notes: River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Your guide will have radio contact with other guides to locate crossing activity. Photography tip: use a zoom lens (200–400mm) and fast shutter speed for action shots. Wear neutral-coloured clothing to blend with the environment.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk — spend a half-day with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Maasai Mara. Learn about their semi-nomadic lifestyle, warrior traditions, and cattle-herding culture. Participate in a traditional jumping dance (adumu), visit a manyatta (homestead), and browse handcrafted beadwork and jewellery at fair prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the reserve for an afternoon game drive with a focus on the Mara's birdlife — over 570 species recorded, including the lilac-breasted roller, martial eagle, and secretary bird. Visit a hippo pool for close-up hippo and crocodile viewing. Return to camp by 17:30.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire storytelling session at the lodge — your Maasai guide shares folklore, constellation navigation, and wildlife tales around a traditional fire. Dinner follows.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the lodge — yoghurt, granola, fresh juice, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Maasai village or back at the lodge — traditional Kenyan staples such as githeri (maize and beans) or chapati with vegetables
meals.dinner: BBQ dinner at the lodge boma (outdoor dining area) — nyama choma, roasted corn, and local accompaniments with Tusker beer or fresh passion fruit juice; budget KES 2,500–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Bring a small gift for the Maasai community such as sugar, flour, or school supplies — check with your lodge for appropriate contributions. Bargaining for crafts is expected but do so respectfully. The cultural visit typically costs USD 20–40 per person and supports community conservation initiatives.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara early and drive north to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 3.5–4 hours via Narok and Nakuru town). Check in to your mid-range lodge or tented camp near the lake shores. Freshen up and have lunch before the afternoon activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — explore the UNESCO World Heritage Site shores of Lake Nakuru. Witness the breathtaking pink spectacle of thousands of lesser and greater flamingos lining the alkaline lake shores. Also look for white rhinos, Rothschild's giraffes, and waterbuck within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the lake viewpoint at Baboon Cliff for panoramic views over Lake Nakuru and the surrounding Rift Valley. Return to your lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Mara lodge before departure — packed or quick cooked breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at your Nakuru lodge upon arrival — buffet or à la carte; budget KES 1,500–2,500
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge restaurant — fresh lake tilapia, Kenyan pilau rice, and sukuma wiki (collard greens); budget KES 2,000–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers fluctuate depending on water levels and algae availability — July is generally a good time. The park also offers excellent rhino tracking opportunities. Park entry fee is approximately USD 60 per person per day. The drive from Mara to Nakuru passes through scenic highland tea country.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive inside Lake Nakuru National Park. Focus on finding the park's resident black and white rhinos — Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's best rhino sanctuaries. Also look for leopards resting in fever trees, buffalo herds, and the abundant birdlife including African fish eagles and pelicans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hyrax Hill Prehistoric Site near Nakuru town (optional cultural detour) — a fascinating archaeological site with Iron Age settlements and a small museum. Alternatively, relax at your lodge and enjoy the pool or take a guided nature walk on the property.
day_by_day.evening: Drive into Nakuru town for an authentic local dining experience at a mid-range restaurant. Explore the lively town centre briefly before returning to the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the lodge — eggs, bacon, toast, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch inside the national park or at the lodge — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Nakuru restaurant — try mutura (Kenyan sausage), nyama choma, and ugali at a budget-friendly eatery; budget KES 800–1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park is fully fenced, making wildlife sightings reliable and safe for self-drive. However, a guided game drive is recommended for the best experience. Carry a fleece or light jacket — Nakuru sits at 1,754m elevation and mornings can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Lake Nakuru and drive south to Ol Pejeta Conservancy near Nanyuki (approximately 3 hours). Check in to your mid-range tented camp or lodge on the conservancy. Enjoy a brief orientation and lunch before the afternoon activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and pay a moving tribute to the last two northern white rhinos (Najin and Fatu) under 24-hour armed guard. Track black rhinos on foot with an expert ranger — an intimate and thrilling wildlife encounter unlike any vehicle safari.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a scenic spot on the conservancy overlooking the Aberdare Range and Mount Kenya. Return to camp for dinner and a briefing on tomorrow's chimpanzee sanctuary visit.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Nakuru lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Ol Pejeta lodge upon arrival — light salads, sandwiches, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Dinner at the conservancy lodge — enjoy a hearty three-course meal with game meat options (eland or ostrich) or vegetarian alternatives; budget KES 3,000–4,500

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy entrance fee is approximately USD 90 per person per day (includes rhino tracking). The northern white rhino enclosure visit has a separate fee of USD 10–15 which directly funds conservation. The conservancy also houses a chimpanzee sanctuary — consider adding this to Day 8 morning. Book rhino tracking in advance as group sizes are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive on Ol Pejeta Conservancy — one of the few places in Kenya where you can see all of the Big Five (lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino) in one conservancy. The open grasslands and acacia woodlands provide excellent visibility. Also visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary — the only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, rescued from across Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your lodge for lunch and a relaxed afternoon. Optional: guided nature walk on the conservancy with a Maasai ranger to learn about tracking, medicinal plants, and ecosystem management. Alternatively, visit the Morani Information Centre to learn about Ol Pejeta's conservation model.
day_by_day.evening: Night game drive on Ol Pejeta (available at most camps) — spot nocturnal species including leopard, serval, spring hare, and African wild cat under the vast Kenyan sky. Return to camp for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at camp before the morning drive — eggs, sausages, fresh fruit, and Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge — buffet with salads, grilled chicken, and local stews
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the lodge after the night drive — hearty soup, main course, and dessert; budget KES 2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: Night game drives must be pre-booked with your camp and typically cost an additional USD 30–50 per person. Ol Pejeta is also a working cattle ranch — you may see Boran cattle herds managed alongside wildlife, a unique conservation-ranching model. Mount Kenya is often visible on clear mornings from the conservancy.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta and drive south to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours via Nairobi ring road or A104 highway). The journey passes through the scenic Rift Valley and the foothills of Mount Kilimanjaro. Check in to your mid-range lodge or tented camp in Amboseli upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views — begin your Amboseli experience with an afternoon game drive. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds, with individuals easily identified by researchers. The backdrop of snow-capped Kilimanjaro (5,895m) on a clear afternoon is one of Africa's most iconic views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Observation Hill inside Amboseli National Park — a short walk to the top offers a sweeping 360-degree panorama of the park, elephant herds, swamps, and Kilimanjaro at golden hour. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Ol Pejeta lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a mid-range restaurant in Nairobi or along the highway — try a local café for pilau or biryani; budget KES 600–1,200
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli lodge — enjoy Swahili-inspired cuisine with coconut fish curry, rice, and fresh mango dessert; budget KES 2,500–3,500

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Amboseli is long — consider breaking it with a 1-hour lunch stop in Nairobi or Emali town. Alternatively, a 45-minute charter flight from Nanyuki to Amboseli airstrip is available for an additional cost. Kilimanjaro is clearest in the early morning and late afternoon — clouds typically build by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Final dawn game drive in Amboseli National Park — the best time to photograph elephants with Kilimanjaro as a backdrop. The Amboseli elephants are remarkably relaxed around vehicles, allowing for intimate close-up encounters. Also look for lions, cheetahs, and large flocks of flamingos in the park's seasonal swamps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for checkout and a farewell lunch. Begin your transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 4 hours) for your onward flight, or if departing later, enjoy a final stop at the Nairobi National Museum or a craft market such as Kazuri Beads or Utamaduni for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10 days of Kenya's finest wildlife, landscapes, and cultural experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — full cooked spread with eggs, tropical fruits, pastries, and Kenyan tea or coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the Amboseli lodge or en route in Nairobi — try a mid-range restaurant such as Carnivore (Nairobi) for a memorable last meal; budget KES 2,000–4,000
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 4 hours from Amboseli to reach Nairobi airport comfortably, accounting for traffic. Tip your safari guides and lodge staff before departure — 10–15% of total safari cost or USD 10–20 per guide per day is standard and greatly appreciated. Keep USD 50 in cash for airport departure tax if not pre-paid. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs purchased comply with CITES regulations — no ivory, rhino horn, or live animals.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Guided game drives allow you to observe elephants, giraffes, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species in open savannah landscapes with iconic snow-capped mountain views.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided walking safaris and jeep tours let you track rhinos on foot with expert rangers, offering an intimate and educational wildlife conservation experience unlike any traditional game drive.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Discover the breathtaking pink shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting millions of flamingos along with pelicans, African fish eagles, and over 450 bird species. The park also shelters white and black rhinos, lions, leopards, and Rothschild giraffes in a compact and highly rewarding ecosystem.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk
experiences.description: Spend a half-day with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Maasai Mara to learn about their ancient wildlife coexistence practices, traditional medicine from native plants, and warrior customs. A guided bush walk with a Maasai elder reveals how to track animals, identify edible plants, and understand the deep cultural connection between the Maasai people and Kenya's wildlife.
experiences.location: Maasai Villages, Narok County border of Maasai Mara

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to depart airport promptly after customs and baggage collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury 4x4 transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours via scenic Rift Valley viewpoints). En route stop at the Great Rift Valley Viewpoint for panoramic photographs and a chilled welcome drink prepared by your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique lodge in Maasai Mara as the sun sets over the savannah. Welcome cocktails and a personalized orientation with your dedicated safari concierge. Settle into your luxury suite and enjoy a candlelit bush dinner under the stars at the lodge's private outdoor dining area.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge dining prior to landing
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the lodge, enjoyed at the Rift Valley Viewpoint stopover — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, Kenyan cheeses, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private candlelit bush dinner at the lodge — slow-roasted Kenyan lamb, seasonal vegetables, and a curated selection of South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passport, visa documentation, and yellow fever certificate are ready for arrival. Lodge will have a representative waiting at the arrivals hall with a name board. Luggage limit on light aircraft transfers is typically 15 kg soft-sided bags — confirm with lodge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at 06:00 in a private open-top 4x4 Land Cruiser with expert Maasai guide. Witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles moving across the Mara plains. Prime season for dramatic Mara River crossings with crocodile action.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration safari deep into the Mara Triangle for afternoon game drives. Look for the Big Five — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino — as predators follow the migrating herds. Enjoy a gourmet bush lunch served in the field beside the Mara River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by 18:30 for sundowner cocktails on the private deck overlooking the savannah. Relax with a signature Mara Sunset G&T. Dinner at the lodge's main dining room featuring a themed 'Bush to Table' menu.

meals.breakfast: Full safari breakfast at the lodge — eggs cooked to order, fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan single-origin coffee, and freshly baked breads served on the open veranda
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush lunch in the field beside the Mara River — charcuterie boards, grilled chicken skewers, quinoa salads, fresh juices, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Bush to Table dinner at the lodge — pan-seared Nile perch with coconut cream sauce, ugali, sautéed sukuma wiki, and a decadent chocolate fondant dessert

day_by_day.notes: Depart lodge by 06:00 to maximize golden-hour wildlife sightings. Wear neutral-colored layers — mornings can be cool at 14–16°C before warming to 25°C by midday. High-quality binoculars provided by the lodge; bring personal camera with telephoto lens.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury hot-air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at dawn — drift silently above the Great Migration herds, vast golden plains, and winding Mara River as the sun rises. One of Africa's most iconic and unforgettable experiences. Flight duration approximately 1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-balloon champagne bush breakfast in the field — a quintessential Mara tradition. Afternoon at leisure at the lodge: enjoy the infinity pool overlooking the savannah, indulge in a signature African botanical spa treatment (e.g., Maasai ochre body wrap or hot stone massage).
day_by_day.evening: Guided sunset walking safari with a senior Maasai tracker and armed ranger around the lodge's private conservancy — learn to read animal tracks, identify bird calls, and understand the ecosystem at ground level. Return for a private dinner in your suite.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the Mara plains post-balloon — smoked salmon blinis, scrambled eggs, fresh fruit platters, pastries, and Moët & Chandon champagne
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the lodge — mezze platter, grilled prawns, avocado salad, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.dinner: Private in-suite romantic dinner — Maasai-spiced beef tenderloin, roasted root vegetables, red wine jus, and a Kenyan honey and cardamom panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon must be booked well in advance — lodge concierge will confirm reservation. Balloon flights are weather-dependent and depart at approximately 05:30. Weight limits apply; confirm with operator. Spa treatments should be pre-booked on arrival day.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk — spend a half-day with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Maasai Mara. Participate in a traditional welcome ceremony, learn about Maasai customs, beadwork, and medicinal plants. Walk the bush with a Maasai elder who shares generations of ecological knowledge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for lunch. Afternoon game drive focusing on predator behavior — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are highly active in the Mara during July. Your private guide will use radio networks with other guides to locate key sightings efficiently.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private sundowner experience at a scenic Mara escarpment lookout point — your butler sets up a bespoke drinks station with artisan canapés as you watch the sky transform over the Rift Valley. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lodge veranda breakfast — full cooked breakfast with Kenyan chai, fresh mango and papaya, yogurt with local honey, and sourdough toast
meals.lunch: Lodge dining room lunch — roasted vegetable tart, lemon herb grilled tilapia, and a fresh garden salad with passion fruit vinaigrette
meals.dinner: Lodge communal dining experience — a shared feast of slow-cooked nyama choma (roasted meat), pilau rice, kachumbari salad, and traditional Kenyan desserts with live Maasai music performance

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly and respectfully for the Maasai village visit — avoid revealing clothing. Small gifts such as school supplies for village children are welcomed and can be arranged through the lodge. Confirm cultural visit timing with lodge concierge as schedules vary.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private game drive in the Mara North Conservancy — a less-visited, exclusive area offering intimate wildlife encounters without the crowds of the main reserve. Exceptional for big cat sightings, particularly leopard and serval. Depart at 06:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter light aircraft flight from Mara Keekorok or Ol Kiombo airstrip to Amboseli National Park (approximately 45 minutes). Check in to a luxury tented camp at Amboseli with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Afternoon Amboseli Elephant Watching safari — home to Africa's largest elephant herds.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a private Kilimanjaro viewpoint as the evening light turns the snow-capped peak golden-pink. Return to camp for a welcome dinner at the Amboseli lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-drive light breakfast at the Mara lodge — granola, yogurt, fresh fruit, and Kenyan coffee. Full breakfast served on return
meals.lunch: In-flight or light snack box provided for charter flight. Arrival lunch at Amboseli camp — grilled chicken wrap, mixed greens, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Amboseli luxury camp — Tanzanian-inspired slow-cooked lamb tagine, couscous, roasted vegetables, and a Kenyan coffee crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Pack a soft-sided bag for the light aircraft transfer — maximum 15 kg. The charter flight offers spectacular aerial views of the Rift Valley and Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is best known for its elephants and Kilimanjaro backdrop — mornings offer the clearest mountain views before clouds build.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views — depart at 06:00 for the best Kilimanjaro visibility and elephant activity. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's most studied elephant families. Your guide will introduce you to specific family groups by name and share decades of behavioral research.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive exploring Amboseli's diverse ecosystems — swamps, open plains, and acacia woodlands. Look for lions, cheetahs, hippos in the swamp, and over 400 bird species. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic 360-degree view of the park and Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night game drive (where permitted) or star-gazing session with a resident astronomer — Amboseli's dark skies offer exceptional views of the Milky Way and Southern Cross. Return to camp for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast in the field with Kilimanjaro backdrop — freshly brewed coffee, egg muffins, smoked salmon, and fresh tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch at Observation Hill — cold cuts, artisan breads, Kenyan cheeses, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the camp restaurant — seared duck breast with tamarind glaze, sweet potato mash, wilted spinach, and a Kenyan vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning before 10:00 — prioritize photography at dawn. Amboseli can be dusty; bring a buff/scarf for game drives. The elephant research guides at the camp can provide extraordinary insight into individual elephant personalities and family dynamics.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter light aircraft from Amboseli to Lake Nakuru (via Wilson Airport or direct, approximately 1–1.5 hours). Check in to a luxury lodge on the shores of Lake Nakuru. Morning Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — witness the breathtaking pink shores of this UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for hosting hundreds of thousands of flamingos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — one of Kenya's best parks for rhino sightings (both black and white), Rothschild's giraffe, and large lion prides. The park is fully fenced, offering excellent predator-prey dynamics. Visit the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for sweeping lake panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat excursion on Lake Nakuru (where available) or sundowner at Baboon Cliff. Return to lodge for dinner overlooking the lake.

meals.breakfast: Final Amboseli breakfast at the camp — full cooked breakfast with fresh juices and Kenyan coffee before transfer to airstrip
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Lake Nakuru lodge — grilled Nile perch, roasted vegetable medley, and fresh passion fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Lakeside dinner at the lodge — slow-roasted Kenyan beef sirloin, truffle mashed potatoes, glazed carrots, and a dark chocolate and Amarula mousse

day_by_day.notes: Flamingo numbers at Lake Nakuru fluctuate based on algae levels — your guide will provide current conditions. Lake Nakuru NP is one of Kenya's best rhino sanctuaries; white rhino sightings are almost guaranteed. Bring a wide-angle lens for the flamingo panoramas.

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — private charter or luxury road transfer from Lake Nakuru to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Arrive for a guided rhino tracking experience — visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and the home of the last two northern white rhinos, Najin and Fatu, under 24-hour armed guard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in Ol Pejeta — the conservancy also hosts chimpanzees (rescued from Central Africa), lions, elephants, and vast herds of plains game. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary for a guided chimpanzee viewing experience — unique in Kenya.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a scenic Ol Pejeta viewpoint with Mount Kenya visible on clear evenings. Check in to a luxury tented camp within the conservancy. Welcome dinner at the camp.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge — continental spread, fresh fruits, and Kenyan chai before transfer
meals.lunch: Bush lunch at Ol Pejeta — grilled chicken, roasted sweet potatoes, mixed salads, and freshly squeezed juices served in the field
meals.dinner: Ol Pejeta camp dinner — wood-fired lamb chops with rosemary and garlic, roasted heritage vegetables, and a Kenyan cardamom and coconut rice pudding with mango compote

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino experience at Ol Pejeta is profoundly moving — there are only two left on Earth, both female. Your guide will provide full conservation context. Ol Pejeta is also one of Kenya's most progressive conservation models — ask about their community and anti-poaching programs.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Mount Kenya foothills nature walk with a specialist naturalist guide from Ol Pejeta — explore the diverse flora and fauna of the conservancy's riverine forests and open grasslands. Look for rare species including aardvark, pangolin tracks, and striped hyena. Depart at 06:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury road transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 3.5 hours). Check in to a five-star Nairobi hotel (e.g., Hemingways Nairobi or The Emakoko). Afternoon at leisure — optional visit to the Giraffe Centre to hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes, or the David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage for a behind-the-scenes keeper experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants — a celebration of your Kenya journey with a curated tasting menu and premium wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan single-origin pour-over coffee, and freshly baked croissants
meals.lunch: En route to Nairobi — stop at a scenic lodge or restaurant in Nanyuki for a light lunch of grilled trout, garden salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting dinner at Hemingways Nairobi or Talisman Restaurant — 6-course Kenyan-inspired tasting menu with wine pairing featuring East African and South African labels

day_by_day.notes: The David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage requires advance booking for the exclusive keeper-for-a-day experience — arrange through your concierge. Nairobi traffic can be significant in the afternoon; allow extra transfer time. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning in Nairobi — optional visit to the Karen Blixen Museum (immortalized in 'Out of Africa') for a guided tour of the colonial farmhouse and gardens. Alternatively, browse the Utamaduni Craft Centre or Kazuri Beads workshop for premium Kenyan souvenirs and handcrafted jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with ample time before departure. Final Kenyan coffee and pastry at the airport's premium lounge. Departure and farewell to Kenya.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight — journey home with extraordinary memories of the Maasai Mara Great Migration, Amboseli elephants, Lake Nakuru flamingos, and Ol Pejeta's last northern white rhinos.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full buffet spread with live cooking stations, fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan teas and coffees, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or airport lounge — club sandwich, Kenyan avocado salad, and a final glass of passion fruit juice
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5 hours before departure for international check-in, immigration, and security at JKIA. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no ivory, coral, or protected species products. Your lodge concierge can assist with curated, legally compliant souvenir recommendations throughout the trip.
